summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would authorise funding from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for government activities outside ordinary annual services, including capital spending and payments to other governments.
It would provide broadly seven months of annual funding, plus Budget measures, alongside supply legislation covering the earlier part of the financial year.
The appropriations would begin on 1 July 2022 or royal assent, whichever came later, and the legislation would expire on 1 July 2025.
changes: The Finance Minister could allocate up to $3,600 million in urgent additional funding, including $3,000 million restricted to COVID-19 expenditure.
Responsible ministers could set payment conditions, amounts and timing for grants to states, territories and local governments.
Appropriated money could be transferred to special accounts where their purposes matched those of the appropriation.
summary.affected: Commonwealth departments, government entities, the Finance Minister and state, territory and local governments would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: The Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2022‑2023 proposes $13.3 billion in spending, including $7.7 billion for Defence, $3.9 billion for infrastructure, and $495 million for Airservices Australia, with a $3 billion Advance to the Finance Minister for COVID‑19 measures and $600 million for other urgent expenditure.
